page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 1890 GB of local disk space, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores also rank in the top 25 percent, indicating efficient parallel processing capabilities. However, multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and software compilation with Clang fall into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests, including large-block read and write operations, consistently register average performance, as do database operations and Redis SET throughput.

The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector and neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA_NI). These instructions contribute to strong performance in image processing, text processing, and small-model LLM inference, where prompt processing and text generation for a 135M model rank in the top 25 percent. For larger workloads, such as medium 7B and large 70B model inference, performance scales down to average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute power with substantial local storage. This configuration is suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, text and image processing pipelines, and moderate database operations that benefit from local NVMe storage without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.
